observation_summary: The compiler fails to resolve typedefs when they are defined within a goog.scope block, resulting in a 'JSC_TYPE_PARSE_ERROR: Bad type annotation. Unknown type' error.
hypothesis: The alias resolution logic in ScopedAliases was incorrectly performing a simple string replacement of the alias name, failing to account for the full qualified name of the aliased object when the type reference was a property access (e.g., c.MyType).
prediction: The fix will involve changing the AliasedTypeNode to store the original alias definition node and performing a more robust replacement of the alias prefix with the full qualified name during the alias application phase.
experiment_rationale: The diff shows that AliasedTypeNode was updated to store the aliasDefinition node instead of just the pre-computed string. The applyAlias method was rewritten to replace the alias prefix with the full qualified name of the alias definition, confirming that the original logic was an insufficient algorithmic implementation for resolving nested type references.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an algorithmic failure in how the compiler resolves aliased types within a scope. The original implementation used a simple string replacement that did not correctly handle qualified names, which is a procedural logic error. The fix involves updating the data structure (AliasedTypeNode) and the logic (applyAlias) to correctly perform the substitution, which fits the definition of an Algorithm/Method defect.
evidence_used: The diff shows a change in the AliasedTypeNode class structure to store the aliasDefinition node.
The diff shows a change in the applyAlias method to use aliasDefinition.getQualifiedName() and replace the alias prefix with the full qualified name.
The bug report indicates that typedefs are not being resolved correctly when inside a goog.scope, which is a procedural resolution task.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not a mismatch between components or an API contract violation, but rather an internal procedural failure in how the compiler resolves names within a scope.
This is not a missing design capability; the capability to resolve aliases exists, but the algorithm used to perform the resolution was incorrect for certain cases.
